creator: flourhands
title: No-Knead Bread
description: Eighteen hours of doing nothing, then forty-five minutes in a hot pot. Best bread-to-effort ratio there is.
steps: Stir the flour, yeast and salt together, add the water, and mix to a shaggy wet dough. No kneading.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 18 hours, until the surface is covered in bubbles.
Tip onto a floured surface, fold it over on itself twice, and rest 15 minutes.
Shape into a ball, put it seam side down on floured baking paper, and prove 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 240C with a lidded casserole inside for 30 minutes.
Lower the dough in on its paper, cover, and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more, until deep brown and hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool completely on a rack before cutting, however hard that is.

creator: flourhands
title: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Brown the butter and chill the dough overnight. Both steps are annoying and both are worth it.
steps: Melt the butter over medium heat and keep cooking for 6 minutes, swirling, until the solids are brown and it smells of toffee. Cool 15 minutes.
Beat in both sugars, then the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate and salt, then the chocolate.
Chill the dough for at least 12 hours — this is where the flavour comes from.
Heat the oven to 180C and scoop golfball-sized mounds well apart on lined trays.
Bake 11 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set and the middles still look underdone.
Leave on the tray 5 minutes to finish, then sprinkle with flaky salt.

creator: flourhands
title: Rosemary Focaccia
description: Dimple it hard enough that your fingers hit the tin. Timid dimples give you flatbread.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water to a very wet dough and leave 10 minutes.
Fold the dough over on itself four times in the bowl, then rest 30 minutes. Repeat this three times.
Oil a deep tray generously and tip the dough in. Cover and prove 2 hours, until doubled and wobbling.
Heat the oven to 220C.
Pour over 3 tbsp oil and press your fingers straight down through the dough to the tin, all over.
Scatter with rosemary and flaky salt.
Bake 25 minutes, until deep gold top and bottom. Lift it out of the tin immediately.

creator: flourhands
title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
description: Prick it all over and pour the syrup on while both are hot, or it sits on top and sets into a crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 170C and line a loaf tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 5 minutes, until pale and noticeably lighter.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between each.
Fold in the flour and lemon zest.
Bake for 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the top has cracked.
Mix the granulated sugar with the lemon juice — it should stay grainy.
Prick the hot cake all over with a skewer and spoon the drizzle over slowly.
Cool in the tin so the syrup soaks back in.

creator: flourhands
title: Overnight Cinnamon Rolls
description: Shape them at night, prove them in the fridge, bake them before anyone is properly awake.
steps: Mix the flour, caster sugar, yeast and 1 tsp salt, then add the warm milk, egg and 3 tbsp butter.
Knead for 8 minutes, until smooth and springy, then prove 1 hour until doubled.
Roll into a large rectangle about 1cm thick.
Spread with the remaining butter and scatter with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long side and cut into 12 with a length of thread.
Sit them in a lined tin, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Take them out an hour before baking, then bake at 180C for 28 minutes, until golden and 90C in the middle.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar and spread it over while warm.

creator: flourhands
title: Black Banana Bread
description: The bananas have to be genuinely black. Yellow bananas make a bland cake.
steps: Heat the oven to 170C and line a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas until almost liquid — lumps make wet patches.
Stir in the melted butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the dry ingredients until only just combined. Overmixing makes it tough.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs and no wet batter.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes before turning out.

creator: flourhands
title: Proper Scones
description: Cold butter, a light hand, and never twist the cutter. Twisting seals the edge and they rise lopsided.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C.
Rub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder and sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Add the milk and bring it together with a knife, then your hands, as briefly as possible.
Pat out to 3cm thick — thinner and they will not rise properly.
Cut straight down with a floured cutter and lift without twisting.
Glaze the tops only, keeping egg off the sides, and bake 14 minutes until risen and golden.

creator: flourhands
title: Dark Chocolate Tart
description: The filling never goes near the oven. It sets in the fridge and stays glossy.
steps: Line a 23cm tart tin with the pastry and chill 30 minutes.
Blind bake at 190C for 15 minutes with beans, then 10 minutes without, until dry and sandy. Cool completely.
Heat the cream and milk until steaming — do not let them boil.
Pour over the chopped chocolate and leave 2 minutes without touching it.
Stir from the middle outwards until glossy, then beat in the butter.
Pour into the case and leave at room temperature for 3 hours to set. The fridge dulls the shine.
Finish with flaky salt.

creator: flourhands
title: Apple and Oat Crumble
description: Bramleys collapse and Coxes hold their shape. Use both and you get sauce and pieces.
steps: Heat the oven to 190C.
Cook the apples with the caster sugar, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water over medium heat for 8 minutes, until the Bramleys start to collapse.
Tip into a baking dish and leave to cool slightly.
Rub the butter into the flour until crumbly, then stir in the oats and demerara.
Scatter over without pressing down — pressed crumble bakes into a lid.
Bake 35 minutes, until the top is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.

creator: flourhands
title: Berry Pavlova
description: Cool it in the switched-off oven with the door shut. Sudden cold is what cracks it.
steps: Heat the oven to 150C and draw a 20cm circle on baking paper.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time, whisking for 8 minutes total.
It is ready when you cannot feel sugar grains between your fingers.
Fold in the vinegar and cornflour.
Spread inside the circle, building the sides higher than the middle.
Turn the oven down to 120C and bake 90 minutes, then switch it off and leave the door shut until cold.
Fill with cream and berries no more than an hour before serving.

creator: flourhands
title: Brioche Burger Buns
description: A wet, sticky dough that becomes the softest bun there is. Use a mixer if you have one.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and 2 eggs and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Add the butter a cube at a time, kneading until each disappears. It will look broken before it comes together — keep going, about 10 minutes.
Prove 1 hour 30 minutes, until doubled, then chill 1 hour to firm it up for shaping.
Divide into eight, roll tight, and space well on a lined tray.
Prove 1 hour, until puffy and slow to spring back.
Glaze with the last egg and bake at 190C for 18 minutes, until deep gold and 90C inside.

creator: flourhands
title: Chocolate Babka
description: Freeze the shaped loaf for ten minutes before cutting it lengthways. Cold dough stays neat.
steps: Make a soft enriched dough with the flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, milk and butter. Knead 8 minutes.
Prove 1 hour, then chill at least 4 hours — cold dough is the only way to roll this thin.
Melt the chocolate with the filling butter and cocoa and cool until spreadable.
Roll the dough to a large rectangle, spread the filling, and roll up tightly from the long edge.
Freeze 10 minutes, then cut the roll in half lengthways and twist the two halves together, cut sides up.
Lower into a lined loaf tin and prove 1 hour.
Bake at 180C for 40 minutes, until dark and 90C in the centre. Brush with sugar syrup while hot.

creator: flourhands
title: Salted Shortbread
description: Three ingredients and one rule: do not let the butter warm up. Chill it twice.
steps: Beat the cold butter with the sugar just until combined — no more.
Work in the flour and salt until it clumps together.
Press into a lined 20cm square tin and chill 30 minutes.
Score into fingers and prick each one twice with a fork.
Chill again for 15 minutes, then bake at 150C for 35 minutes, until pale gold at the edges only.
Cut along the scores while hot, sprinkle with salt, and cool in the tin.

creator: flourhands
title: Carrot Cake
description: Oil, not butter, which is why it stays moist for four days. Grate the carrots finely.
steps: Heat the oven to 175C and line two 20cm tins.
Whisk the sugar, oil and eggs together for 2 minutes until smooth.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate, cinnamon and 1 tsp salt.
Stir through the carrot and walnuts.
Divide between the tins and bake 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely — icing a warm cake is how you get soup.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar until just smooth and sandwich and top the cake.

creator: flourhands
title: Soft Pretzels
description: The bicarbonate bath is what makes them pretzels rather than bread in a knot.
steps: Make a firm dough and knead 8 minutes until smooth. Prove 1 hour.
Divide into eight, roll each into a 60cm rope, and twist into pretzel shape.
Bring a wide pan of water to the boil and add the bicarbonate carefully — it will foam up.
Poach each pretzel for 30 seconds, turning once, then lift onto a lined tray.
Scatter with flaky salt while wet.
Bake at 220C for 14 minutes, until deep mahogany brown.
Brush with melted butter as they come out.

creator: flourhands
title: Vanilla Panna Cotta
description: Just enough gelatine to hold and no more. It should wobble alarmingly.
steps: Soak the gelatine in cold water for 5 minutes until floppy.
Heat the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla until steaming, then take off the heat and infuse 10 minutes.
Squeeze the gelatine out and stir it in until fully dissolved. Do not boil after this point.
Strain into four moulds and chill at least 4 hours.
Dip each mould in hot water for 3 seconds to turn out.
Serve with the raspberries.

creator: flourhands
title: Fudge Brownies
description: Underbake them. A skewer should come out sticky, not clean, or you have made cake.
steps: Heat the oven to 175C and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in both sugars, then the eggs one at a time, beating for a full minute after the last — this makes the shiny crust.
Fold in the flour and cocoa until just combined.
Bake 24 minutes. The middle should still wobble slightly and a skewer should come out sticky.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting, then sprinkle with salt.

creator: flourhands
title: Tiramisu
description: No baking, no gelatine. Dip the biscuits fast — one second a side or they collapse.
steps: Whisk the yolks and sugar over a pan of simmering water for 6 minutes, until thick and pale and hot to the touch.
Cool for 10 minutes, then beat in the mascarpone until smooth.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it through.
Mix the coffee and marsala in a shallow dish.
Dip each biscuit for one second a side only and layer them in a dish.
Spread over half the cream, then repeat.
Chill at least 6 hours, and dust with cocoa only just before serving.

creator: flourhands
title: Cold-Ferment Pizza Dough
description: Three days in the fridge. It is the only thing that gets you that blistered, chewy edge at home.
steps: Mix everything to a rough dough and leave 20 minutes.
Knead for 5 minutes, until smooth, then divide into four and roll each into a tight ball.
Put each in its own covered container and refrigerate for 3 days.
Take them out 2 hours before baking.
Heat the oven and a steel or heavy tray as hot as it goes, at least 30 minutes.
Stretch each ball by hand from the middle out, leaving the rim untouched.
Top sparingly and bake 7 to 9 minutes, until the crust is blistered and charred in spots.

creator: flourhands
title: Bakewell Tart
description: Frangipane over jam. Chill the pastry case properly or the jam boils through the bottom.
steps: Line a 23cm tin with the pastry and chill 30 minutes.
Blind bake at 190C for 15 minutes with beans, then 8 minutes without.
Spread the jam over the cooled base.
Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the ground almonds and extract.
Spread over the jam carefully and scatter with flaked almonds.
Bake at 175C for 35 minutes, until golden and firm in the middle.
Cool completely before cutting.
